div.l: Me thynketh it a cordaunt to resoun
To telle ȝow / al the conchusyoun condition conchusyoun condition
Of eche of hem as it semyth me
And whiche þey were ⁊and of what degre
And ek in what aray þᵗat they were inne
And at a knyȝt þānne wele I ferst begynne
Miles¶ A knyght þere was ⁊and that a worthy man Knyth
That from the tyme that he ferst began
To rydyn out he louede Chyualrye
Trouthe honour fredom ⁊and curteysie
Ful worthi was he in hese lordis werre
And therto hadde he / redyn noman ferre
As wel in cristyndōm as in hethnesse
And euere honoured for hese worthynesse
¶ At Alisandir he was whan it was wonne
And ofte tyme / he hadde þe bord begunne
Abouyn alle nacyoūnmys in Pruce
In lectowe hadde he reysed ⁊and in reuce
Nōn cristene man so ofte / of his degre
In gernage at þe sege ek hadde he be
Of Algazer / ⁊and redyn in balmarye
At leyeys was he ⁊and at satalye
Whan they were wonne ⁊and in þe grete see
At manye anobil aryue hadde he be
At mortal bataylis hadde he be fiftene
And for oure feith at tramessene
In lystis thryis / ⁊and ay slayen his fo
This ilke worthi knyth hadde ben also
Sūmtyme with þe lord of Palatye
Ageyn anothir hethen / in Turkye
And eủeremor he hadde a soủereyn prys
And thow that he were worthy he was wys
And of hese port as meke as is a mayde
He neủere ȝit nōn velany ne sayde
In al his lyȝf vn to no maner wight
He was a weray ꝑperfit gentil knyȝt
